::: {.why}
Five model families, one test period, one cost model, one portfolio construction, and the number that comes out is the one milestone 7 reports whichever way it falls.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Run every model on the same test set with the same costs and report out-of-sample performance with intervals.
- Report the result identically regardless of which model won.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Execute the audit: linear baseline, boosting, forest, network, and the seed-ensemble average of all of them, each producing a portfolio through the same construction with the same costs. Report out-of-sample R-squared, information ratio and net information ratio with intervals for each.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Put the differences in context before interpreting them: compare every pairwise difference against the across-seed spread from day 227 and against the interval width. Mark which differences are distinguishable and which are not. Most will not be, and that is the finding.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The audit runs once on the frozen protocol and produces the phase's headline comparison, with every pairwise difference tested against the seed spread rather than read off a leaderboard.
:::

## Resources

- [Gu, Kelly & Xiu (2020) — Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning](https://dachxiu.chicagobooth.edu/download/ML.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The audit results table with intervals and a marked column showing which pairwise differences are distinguishable.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Which model won, by how much, and is that difference larger than your seed spread?
:::
